items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: I think -- it's my opinion that Milt Gabler, who was putting it out on Commodore, got Leonard to do this

ctx.x: The record. He says, a sincere piano solo by Art Hodes, Russian-born Art Hodes. Blues flavor and all that. There wasn't a bad thing there. He doesn't say I'm a great pianistic pianist. But there's nothing bad about the rendition.

I think -- it's my opinion that Milt Gabler, who was putting it out on Commodore, got Leonard to do this, and they inserted it. There was ten records reviewed. Mine was the bottom one, by Look. And I don't know if this is true, but I think that it was Milt that got him to do this. This was pre-argument, before this thing.

Another unfortunate thing, I think, came out of that. And I felt that even in Louisville, Kentucky, because musicians were reading this all over the country. The schism that grew between the guys that wanted to play bebop and the guys that wanted to play traditional or whatever.
